Shyam Visweswaran (born 1965) is an Indian American biomedical informatician, physician, and computer scientist, and academic leader known for his work in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in healthcare and clinical decision support. He is the Interim Chair and UPMC Endowed Professor of [https://www.dbmi.pitt.edu/ Biomedical Informatics] at the University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine.
Education
Visweswaran earned his M.B., B.S. (MD equivalent) at the Jawaharlal Institute of Post-Graduate Medical Education and Research (JIPMER) in Puducherry, India. He trained as an anesthesiologist in India and later completed a residency in neurology at Boston University Medical Center. Visweswaran obtained an M.S. in Physiology and Biophysics from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and later completed a Ph.D. in [https://www.isp.pitt.edu/ Intelligent Systems] (Artificial Intelligence) at the University of Pittsburgh.
Career and research
Visweswaran joined the faculty of the [https://www.dbmi.pitt.edu/ Department of Biomedical Informatics] at the University of Pittsburgh in 2007. Throughout his career, he has held numerous academic and administrative roles, including serving as Vice Chair of Clinical Informatics and Director of the Biomedical Informatics Core at the [https://ctsi.pitt.edu/ Clinical and Translational Science Institute] (CTSI). His research focuses on applying AI/ML to biomedicine, with a specific focus on AI/ML-enabled clinical decision support, ethically grounded clinical algorithms, patient-specific modeling and causal discovery from complex biomedical data, research data warehousing, and ontology development.
Visweswaran directs the [http://www.ccai.thevislab.com/ Center for Clinical Artificial Intelligence] (CCAI), which develops, implements, and evaluates high-performance clinical decision support tools powered by AI and ML. He is involved in large-scale efforts such as the [https://joinallofuspa.org/ All of Us Pennsylvania] research program, the [https://www.pediatricsleepnetwork.org/ SleepLife] study, and the [https://enact-network.org/ ENACT] (Evolve to Next-Gen Accrual of patients to Clinical Trials) network. He led the development of a common data model, [https://dbmi-pitt.github.io/ACT-Network/ontology.html i2b2 ontologies], and a COVID-19 ontology for the ENACT network (formerly the ACT network), which connects the electronic health records (EHRs) of over 50 CTSA hubs, providing access to over 140 million patient records. He led the development of the Neptune research data warehouse at the University of Pittsburgh, which contains structured, text, and imaging EHR data, as well as insurance claims data from 40 University of Pittsburgh Medical Center hospitals, with access to 5 million patients.
He contributed to the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, serving as a member of the committee that produced the Consensus Study Report, [https://www.nationalacademies.org/projects/HMD-HSP-22-14 Rethinking Race and Ethnicity in Biomedical Research], and serves on the national [https://encodingequity.org/ Encoding Equity] Inaugural Advisory Committee established by the Council of Medical Specialty Societies. He created a website for [http://www.clinical-algorithms-with-race-and-ethnicity.org/ Clinical Algorithms with Race and Ethnicity] that has been covered in STAT.
Honors
* 2022 – Fellow of the [https://digitalhealth.org.au/ Australasian Institute of Digital Health] (AIDH)
* 2023 – Fellow of the American College of Medical Informatics (ACMI)
* 2024 – Fellow of the [https://imia-medinfo.org/wp/iahsi/ International Academy of Health Sciences Informatics] (IAHSI)
